conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Revenue Officer William Carter, badge ID 84156. To whom am I speaking?
Um, hello, this is Doris Miller. I got a message to call this number about my taxes. Is something wrong?

Ms. Miller, I am contacting you regarding an outstanding compliance issue involving your payroll and 1099 filings for your business, as mandated by federal tax code. Are you aware that your account has been flagged for multiple violations?
No, I don't run a big business, it's just me. I don't think I did anything wrong with my taxes.

According to our records, you failed to submit critical payroll documentation and federal 1099 forms as required. This is a serious breach of IRS regulations and Section 7203 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Oh my, I didn't know anything about that. I always try to pay what I owe. What does this mean?
Ms. Miller, failure to comply with these regulations places you at immediate risk for a federal audit, civil penalties, and possible suspension of your Social Security or Medicare benefits.
Wait, my Social Security? I can't lose that. That's how I pay for everything.
If the matter is not resolved today, legal action may begin. The IRS is authorized to freeze your bank accounts, garnish Social Security payments, and seize assets pending investigation.
No, please, I can't have that happen. What am I supposed to do?

In order to prevent escalation, you must settle your outstanding compliance fee immediately. Standard procedure is to process payment through an IRS-certified electronic method. Do you have access to your bank or a payment app right now?
I have a bank account, but I don't use those fancy apps. Can't I just mail something?

Mailing payments is not an option at this stage. We require an instant settlement to halt enforcement. The fee is $2,380. You may process this using a wire transfer or, if easier, by purchasing government-approved gift cards and relaying the codes to me.
Gift cards? For the IRS? That sounds odd.

Ma'am, these are Treasury-secured payment cards used to expedite compliance. If you do not act, I will be forced to proceed with a federal asset freeze and notification to your benefits administrator.
Oh, I don't want any trouble. Where would I get these cards?
You can purchase them at any large retailer such as Walmart or CVS. You must remain on the line with me throughout the process for verification purposes.
This is really scary. I'm not sure I have enough in my account.
If you cannot pay the full amount now, partial compliance is permitted. Tell me how much you can access immediately so I can update your federal ledger and prevent further penalty.
Maybe $900, I have that for rent and groceries.
That will suffice for now. Go to the nearest store and purchase $900 in Apple or Google Play gift cards. As soon as you have them, read the codes to me without delay or your file will be escalated.
But I need that money for living. Are you sure there's no other way?

Ms. Miller, failure to comply will result in immediate legal action and suspension of all federal benefits. The choice is yours, but this call is your final opportunity to resolve the matter voluntarily.
Okay, okay, I'll go to the store now. Please don't do anything to my Social Security.
Remain on the line. Once you've obtained the cards, I will instruct you step by step to ensure your compliance and close your case.
